question: As per Human Development Report 2021 - 22, what is the female Life Expectancy at birth in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**67.5 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Human Development Report 2021-22, the female life expectancy at birth in India is 67.5 years.
 
• Life expectancy at birth is the average number of years a newborn is expected to live if current mortality rates continue to apply.
 
• Increased life expectancy indicates improvements in healthcare, nutrition, and general living conditions.
 
• Life expectancy is a key indicator used to measure the overall health and well-being of a population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Development Report (HDR)**

 
 
• The Human Development Report is an annual report published by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• It measures development not only through economic growth but also through improvements in health, education, and income.
 
• The HDR uses the Human Development Index (HDI) as a composite statistic of life expectancy, education, and per capita income indicators.
 
• Countries are ranked based on their HDI to assess their development progress.
 
 
 
• **Life Expectancy at Birth**
 
 
• It is an estimate of the average number of years a newborn is expected to live if current mortality rates remain constant throughout their life.
 
• Life expectancy is influenced by factors such as healthcare access, quality of life, and socio-economic conditions.
 
• Higher life expectancy typically correlates with better health care, nutrition, and overall living conditions.
 
• It is a crucial indicator for assessing the effectiveness of public health policies and socio-economic development.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Life Expectancy**
 
 
• Access to healthcare services and quality of medical care.
 
• Living conditions, including housing, sanitation, and nutrition.
 
• Social determinants such as education, income, and employment.
 
• Public health policies and preventative measures.
